Stop reporting reach

By lowob · 23 March 2026 · 3-minute read · Revenue

Pick the few numbers that show attention turning into money that comes back. Instrument them before you spend on growth, report them to everyone who matters, and drop the vanity metrics from the top of the page.

The question every number has to answer

Did someone do something that makes the business more likely to exist next year? If a metric can rise while the answer is no, it belongs in an appendix.

What to measure

Stage Web3 AI Why it matters
Activation First deposit, first trade, first onchain action First task completed, first integration live Interest became use
Retention Deposits and wallets still active at 30 / 90 days Weekly active users or teams at 30 / 90 days Use became habit
Revenue Protocol fees or revenue, net of incentives Paid accounts, net revenue retention Habit became money
Efficiency Cost per retained depositor, incentive spend per $ of sticky TVL Customer acquisition cost, payback period Money exceeds what it cost
Source Which partner, campaign or referral brought them Same Where to spend next

The incentive adjustment

In web3, separate what you paid for from what you earned. Report TVL, volume and users both with and without incentivised activity. If 80% disappears when incentives end, the honest number is the 20%, and investors will compute it whether you do or not.

The same principle applies to AI products running free tiers or heavy discounts. Report the paid and the free separately.

Instrument before you spend

The most expensive mistake in early GTM is a year of activity with no way to tell what worked. Before spending meaningfully on any channel:

Tag every link and referral by source. Track activation and 30-day retention by source, not just in aggregate. For web3, map wallet addresses to campaigns where you can do so properly and lawfully.

Write down what result would make you double the channel and what would make you stop it.

One report, three audiences

The monthly report you send investors should contain the same core numbers your team runs the business on, and a version of it should be what you share with your community. Different detail, same truth. If the investor update and the internal dashboard disagree, one of them is wrong.

What to stop reporting

Impressions and reach, at the top of anything; Follower counts as progress; Waitlist size without a conversion rate.

Incentivised volume without the unincentivised number next to it; "Partnerships announced" without what each one produced.

The checklist

Five numbers: activation, retention, revenue, efficiency, source.

Incentivised and organic reported separately.

Every channel tagged before money goes in.

A stop / double rule for each channel.

One monthly report, the same core numbers for every audience.
